claims.text: Corrosion resistance in steels tailored for chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications is primarily governed by formation of a continuous, self-healing Cr2O3 surface film.
An optimal grain-boundary density promotes rapid repassivation after minor mechanical or chemical disruption.
Increasing chromium content enhances formation of a uniform, adherent chromium oxide layer.
Thermomechanical processing can be used to control grain-boundary density.
The continuity and self-healing capability of the chromium oxide layer are mediated by grain-boundary density.
Chromium enriched at the steel surface preferentially oxidizes to form a thin Cr2O3 layer.
Chromium may segregate at steel grain boundaries.
The Cr2O3 layer acts as a barrier to further corrosive attack.
After local oxide damage, adjacent chromium-rich regions enable rapid repassivation.
An optimal grain-boundary network may facilitate oxide repair by providing diffusion paths for chromium and oxygen.
Steels with higher chromium content and a controlled microstructure will have lower corrosion rates than baseline steels with lower chromium content.
The modified steels will exhibit less pitting and more stable electrochemical potentials than the baseline.
Following cyclic mechanical or chemical damage, the modified steels will reform the protective film rapidly and maintain lower corrosion metrics than the baseline.
Baseline steels with standard chromium content and no microstructural optimization have a less uniform oxide film and a higher corrosion rate.
The proposed mechanism should hold under moderate acidity or chloride concentration and stresses that do not irreversibly damage the oxide or alter the microstructure.
The proposed mechanism may fail under extreme high-temperature oxidation or severe cyclic loading.
The passivating role of Cr2O3 in steels is well established.
The contribution of grain-boundary density to repassivation kinetics under cyclic or extreme conditions is uncertain.
Interactions with alloying elements such as Mo or Ni may modify the proposed mechanism in different steel grades.
